name: VeriSign, Inc.
moat_justification: Textbook wide moat: exclusive ICANN registry rights for .com/.net with presumptive renewal, .com's default-TLD network status and registrant switching costs, contractual 7% pricing power repeatedly exercised, and ~68% operating margins on minimal capex. Scored 9 not 10 because the moat is granted by contract and politics — NTIA/antitrust pressure on .com pricing is a live, binary erosion force at each renewal.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
BUYBACK_TAILWIND: share count shrinking 4.6%/yr — already credited via the growth adjustment
one_liner: Elite wide-moat registry monopoly (9/10) with contractual pricing power — but at $295.38 the price assumes far more than the model gives: weighted IRR 8.16%, weighted IV@15% $123.46; it clears 15% only below ~$123.
moat_for: Exclusive .com/.net registry operator under ICANN agreements with presumptive renewal — no competitor can legally take the registry without a contract change

.com is the default commercial TLD: brand identity, email, and links are embedded in 179.1M registrations — switching costs are borne by registrants, not Verisign, and renewal rates run ~76% despite repeated price hikes

Proven contractual pricing power: wholesale .com price taken from $7.85 to $10.26 since 2021, next +7% to $10.97 effective Nov 1, 2026, with up to three more 7% steps to 2030; .net allows up to 10%/yr
Structural cost advantage: ~68% operating margins, capex of only $22.8M on $1,656.6M FY2025 revenue — registry scale economics no entrant can replicate
29 years of 100% .com/.net DNS availability — operational record is itself a barrier to any re-bid argument
moat_against: Moat is granted by ICANN/NTIA contracts, not owned — .com agreement runs to Nov 2030 and pricing terms are a political/antitrust target (NTIA publicly wanted lower .com prices at the 2024 renewal; antitrust suit filed over .com pricing)
Mature .com base — long-run volume growth depends on new-business formation; alternative TLDs (.ai, ccTLDs), brand TLDs from ICANN's 2026 round, and platform/social presence substitute at the margin
Wholesale price hikes are capped (7% in only 4 of each 6 years for .com) and each hike risks registrar/registrant pushback and volume elasticity
Single-product concentration — essentially all economics are .com/.net registry fees; a DNS security/availability failure would be existential for the contract
